summary: External tool probe mesh causes repeated schema validation round-trips and request timeouts
description:
Issue summary: BrightDocs reports a spike in end-to-end token latency and intermittent request timeouts when invoking external tool integrations from the chat endpoint. The behaviour started after a recent rollout of the tool-proxy mesh (2/28 rollout) and coincides with increased error rates on dedicated pools.

Impact: Multiple production customers using tool/function-calling experience 200ms-2s extra tail latency per request and occasional 504s for long-running chains. This affects critical summarization pipelines and interactive agent flows.

Environment: Dedicated capacity (BrightDocs account), prod-us-east region; traffic routed through tool-proxy mesh and service mesh sidecars. Observed across gptx-13b-v1 and redwood-open-compat-7b serving variants.

Steps to reproduce: 1) Use BrightDocs agent integration to call external-search tool via our standard toolcall schema. 2) Send a typical 200-token chat request with tool invocation. 3) Observe streaming start time and final token latency; repeat at 50 RPS. 4) On failures, check request logs for repeated schema GETs and 504s.

Observed behaviour: The tool-proxy performs multiple sequential schema validation fetches to the tool registry on a per-request path due to cache-miss amplification across mesh hops. Each validation adds a 60-300ms round-trip; chains with two tool calls see compounding delays. When the registry experiences transient latency, requests time out at the API gateway.

Expected behaviour: Tool schema validation should be memoized locally at the tool-proxy with a short TTL and parallelized where safe (single validation per tool per container). End-to-end latency should not include redundant external schema RTTs.

Temporary workaround: 1) Increase tool schema cache TTL for BrightDocs dedicated pools (applied as 2026-03-10 18:12 UTC). 2) For critical routes, enable local in-memory schema cache override via console feature flag. Workaround reduces extra RTTs but does not eliminate underlying race where multiple mesh replicas concurrently miss the cache.
logs: Sample traces: 2026-03-10T17:45:02Z request id=bd-req-9a3f: tool-proxy->registry GET /schema/tool-external-search took 210ms; subsequent GET from next mesh replica 248ms; streaming start delayed by 480ms. API gateway 504s logged for requests with cumulative schema fetch >1.2s. See trace links: https://observability.redwood.ai/trace/bd-req-9a3f and dashboard latency spike graph (Chart ID: TOOLCALL-RT-20260310).
investigation_notes:
Initial hypothesis: cache TTL misconfiguration + mesh replication causes cache stampede. Evidence: request traces show sequential registry hits from distinct mesh replicas for same request chain. CPU/memory on proxies normal; registry error rate increased for short window. Key finding: a recent change (mesh-sidecar start order) made schema cache local to sidecar and not shared, and the startup path triggers immediate validation lookups.

Eng actions so far: - Rolled cache TTL to 30s for affected dedicated pools (2026-03-10 18:12 UTC). - Added guard to deduplicate concurrent schema fetches within a proxy instance (hotfix patch applied to staging, PR linked). - Collecting metrics for cache-miss fanout size and registry latency.

Open questions: - Does caching at proxy level introduce staleness risk for dynamic tools? Need policy. - Should we implement a central in-cluster schema cache to avoid cross-replica amplification?
resolution: In-progress: hotfix PR to deduplicate concurrent schema fetches across requests merged to canary (PR: github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/1982). Cache TTL extended for BrightDocs pools as a stopgap. Follow-ups: implement cluster-level schema cache and add chaos tests for registry latency. No permanent customer-visible fix pushed to all production clusters yet.
